process.name: Develop Conceptual Security Architecture
process.description: Translates contextual business requirements into the conceptual security architecture and establishes the traceability basis for the logical layer.

inputs.name: SABSA Business Attributes Profile (BAP)
inputs.description: Prioritised profile of business attributes with metrics and measures from the contextual layer.
inputs.origin: Inherited from the preceding 'Develop Contextual Security Architecture' process, especially from the contextual WHAT view and the prioritised business attributes profile.

inputs.name: Business Risk Context
inputs.description: Business-level threats, vulnerabilities, and impacts as the basis for the WHY dimension.
inputs.origin: Inherited from the contextual risk and threat baseline of the preceding process, consolidated from business impact, threat, and vulnerability analysis.

inputs.name: Business Drivers & Constraints
inputs.description: Strategic drivers, organisational constraints, and business vision.
inputs.origin: Inherited from business vision, stakeholder goals, guiding constraints, and architecture principles from the strategic and contextual setup.

inputs.name: Compliance & Regulatory Requirements
inputs.description: Relevant legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements.
inputs.origin: Inherited from the compliance baseline, regulatory obligations, contractual requirements, and external obligations in the enterprise context.

outputs.name: WHAT: Business Attributes Taxonomy & Profile with integrated performance targets
outputs.description: Conceptual layer WHAT artefact with prioritised attributes and quantified KPI/KRI targets.

outputs.name: WHY: Enablement & Control Objectives; Policy Architecture; Risk Categories; Risk Management Strategies; Risk Modelling Framework; Assurance Framework
outputs.description: Conceptual layer WHY artefacts for objectives, policy, risk, strategy, and assurance.

outputs.name: HOW: Inventory of all Operational Processes; Process Mapping Framework; Architectural Strategies for IT used in Process Support
outputs.description: Conceptual layer HOW artefacts for process assurance and process-to-objective traceability.

outputs.name: WHERE: Security Domain Concepts & Framework
outputs.description: Conceptual layer WHERE artefact defining security domains and their interactions.

outputs.name: WHO: Owners, Custodians & Users; Service Providers & Customers; Trust Modelling Framework
outputs.description: Conceptual layer WHO artefacts for entities, accountability, and trust.

outputs.name: WHEN: Through-Life Risk Management Framework; Attribute Performance Targets
outputs.description: Conceptual layer WHEN artefacts for lifecycle timing and performance traceability.

steps.name: Step 1 - Synthesize Business Value & Knowledge Strategy
steps.description: Refines business attributes at conceptual level, integrates performance targets, and derives the conceptual business information architecture.

inputs.name: SABSA Business Attributes Profile (BAP)
inputs.description: Validated business attributes profile from the contextual layer.

inputs.name: Stakeholder Expectations & Business Strategy
inputs.description: Stakeholder goals, vision, and performance expectations relevant for the conceptual WHAT perspective.

inputs.name: SABSA Generic Attributes Library
inputs.description: Reference taxonomy used to validate completeness and consistency of the business attributes profile.

outputs.name: Business Attributes Taxonomy & Profile with integrated performance targets
outputs.description: Conceptual WHAT artefact with prioritised business attributes and integrated performance targets.

steps.name: Step 2 - Develop Risk Management Strategy & Objectives
steps.description: Builds conceptual risk management including objectives, policy architecture, risk categories, modelling, and assurance.

inputs.name: Business Attributes Taxonomy & Profile with integrated performance targets
inputs.description: Output from Step 1 and the basis for deriving control objectives.

inputs.name: Business Risk Context
inputs.description: Contextual threats, vulnerabilities, and impacts used for the conceptual WHY perspective.

inputs.name: Compliance & Regulatory Requirements
inputs.description: Relevant regulatory and contractual obligations shaping conceptual policy architecture.

inputs.name: Threat Intelligence (conceptual)
inputs.description: High-level threat landscape used to support conceptual risk categorisation.

outputs.name: Enablement & Control Objectives
outputs.description: Measurable objectives derived from business attributes and traced into the conceptual WHY perspective.

outputs.name: Policy Architecture
outputs.description: Conceptual policy hierarchy linking control objectives, requirements, and governance intent.

outputs.name: Risk Categories
outputs.description: Conceptual risk categories mapped to business attributes and control objectives.

outputs.name: Risk Management Strategies
outputs.description: Conceptual risk treatment strategies aligned to risk appetite and policy direction.

outputs.name: Risk Modelling Framework
outputs.description: Shared conceptual evaluation framework for assessing and comparing risk across layers.

outputs.name: Assurance Framework
outputs.description: Conceptual assurance framework mapping evidence and assurance activities to objectives.

steps.name: Step 3 - Define Strategies for Process Assurance
steps.description: Inventories operational processes, classifies them, and defines process mapping and IT support strategies.

inputs.name: Enablement & Control Objectives
inputs.description: Conceptual control objectives determining which operational processes matter most.

inputs.name: Policy Architecture
inputs.description: Conceptual policy hierarchy defining the scope and criteria for process selection and mapping.

inputs.name: Business Process Inventory (Contextual Layer)
inputs.description: Existing list of business processes used as the starting point for operational process analysis.

inputs.name: Technology Context
inputs.description: High-level technology architecture context supporting the derivation of process-support strategies.

outputs.name: Inventory of all Operational Processes (IT, industrial & manual)
outputs.description: Classified inventory of operational processes across IT, industrial, and manual contexts.

outputs.name: Process Mapping Framework
outputs.description: Traceability framework linking processes to control objectives and business attributes.

outputs.name: Architectural Strategies for IT used in Process Support
outputs.description: Conceptual IT architecture strategies used to support and secure operational processes.

steps.name: Step 4 - Synthesize Domain Framework
steps.description: Identifies, maps, and formalises security domains and their boundaries.

inputs.name: Business Attributes Taxonomy & Profile with integrated performance targets
inputs.description: Business attributes and performance targets defining domain protection needs.

inputs.name: Enablement & Control Objectives
inputs.description: Conceptual objectives shaping the scope and intent of security domains.

inputs.name: Policy Architecture
inputs.description: Conceptual policy structure influencing domain boundaries and control expectations.

inputs.name: Organisation Structure & Locations
inputs.description: Organisational and geographical structure used to identify conceptual security domains.

outputs.name: Security Domain Concepts & Framework
outputs.description: Conceptual domain framework with domain boundaries, interactions, and attribute mappings.

steps.name: Step 5 - Develop Security & Risk Governance; Trust Framework
steps.description: Defines entities, service-provider/customer mappings, accountability, and trust relationships.

inputs.name: Security Domain Concepts & Framework
inputs.description: Conceptual domain model providing the structure for governance and trust allocation.

inputs.name: Enablement & Control Objectives
inputs.description: Objectives that need explicit governance ownership and accountability.

inputs.name: Assurance Framework
inputs.description: Assurance responsibilities used to support entity and governance assignments.

inputs.name: Business Entity Structure
inputs.description: Stakeholders, partners, customers, and organisational entities relevant for classification.

outputs.name: Owners, Custodians & Users
outputs.description: Conceptual entity register with role classification and accountability.

outputs.name: Service Providers & Customers
outputs.description: Conceptual provider and customer map including security responsibilities in the service chain.

outputs.name: Trust Modelling Framework
outputs.description: Conceptual trust model defining trust relationships, levels, and boundaries.

steps.name: Step 6 - Define Time Management Framework
steps.description: Defines lifecycle, timing, and traceability for risk management and performance targets.

inputs.name: Business Attributes Taxonomy & Profile with integrated performance targets
inputs.description: Performance targets that need to be anchored across time and lifecycle perspectives.

inputs.name: Risk Management Strategies
inputs.description: Conceptual risk strategies that need to be sustained through lifecycle planning.

inputs.name: Assurance Framework
inputs.description: Assurance activities that need a conceptual timing and review structure.

inputs.name: Inventory of all Operational Processes
inputs.description: Operational processes used to anchor lifecycle and timing concepts.

outputs.name: Through-Life Risk Management Framework
outputs.description: Conceptual lifecycle framework for risk management including reviews and trigger events.

outputs.name: Attribute Performance Targets
outputs.description: Time-anchored performance targets for attributes as the basis for KPI and KRI monitoring.
